Pascal’s law: A pressure change applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally and undiminished throughout the fluid and to the container walls. Application: a hydraulic press.
Hydraulic brakes work on Pascal’s law: pressure applied to the enclosed brake fluid at the master cylinder is transmitted equally through the fluid to the pistons at the wheels.
The pressure increase is transmitted equally to all parts of the confined liquid. An example is a hydraulic brake system.
